quote: When the Pratiharas' power weakened, three powers emerged. Among these, the Chedis of Kalachuri, the Chandelas of Jaijakabhukti, and the Paramaras of Malwa rise upon the horizon together. In their long span of five centuries, the ambitious Paramara kings extended their boundaries over a large territory. Their kingdom was spread — along with Malwa — up to Vidisha and Udaipur beyond Bhopal, and in the west up to areas like Hansol, Modhasa and Mahudi. book_title: Jagta Hua Kasba / कथा उदयपुर — English translation
quote: But about the Paramaras he mentioned everywhere with respect. He says that in the history of Central India, the Panwar Rajputs are considered more honourable than the other dynasties. But they were defeated by the Muslims, and long ago their kingdom ended. Later, a chieftain of this line got established in his ancestors' capital, Dhar; but he came as an attendant of a Maratha king.
note: Malcolm says the Panwar Rajputs are considered more honourable than other dynasties in Central India; defeated by Muslims; a chieftain later settled in Dhar as a Maratha king's attendant.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event; pages approximate

book_title: Jagta Hua Kasba / कथा उदयपुर — English translation
quote: But Malcolm saw the Paramaras living and residing with much respect even after centuries. He is quite careful in writing about them. He knows that they are descendants of those great Paramara kings, whose golden memories of their splendid reign are spread far and wide in Central India.
note: Malcolm saw Paramara descendants living with respect centuries later, aware of their great ancestors.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event; pages approximate

book_title: Jagta Hua Kasba / कथा उदयपुर — English translation
quote: Worthy of note, too, is that long before the date of the inscription, Devpaldev had already begun sitting upon the royal throne in the capital Dhar and using the full royal titles. Before becoming king, he must have held some military or administrative responsibility in Udaipur itself — and that is why, in this inscription, he is addressed only with the title of *Mahakumar*. If he was in Udaipur before becoming king, then this fact enhances the importance of Udaipur; for, about a hundred and fifty years before him, Udayadity too must have been in some such role. Now this also becomes clear — that Udaipur was such a centre from which at least two crown-princes came forth to become kings in the Paramara dynasty.
note: Devpaldev styled only Mahakumar in the record; author infers he held a role in Udaipur before becoming king, as Udayadity may have, making Udaipur a source of two Paramara kings.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event; pages approximate

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: अपने पाँच शताब्दियों के लम्बे काल में महात्वाकांक्षी परमार राजाओं ने एक बड़े भूभाग पर अपनी सीमाओं का विस्तार किया। उनका राज्य मालवा के साथ भोपाल के आगे विदिशा और उदयपुर तक, पश्चिम में हंसोल, मोढासा, महुडी जैसे इलाकों तक फैला हुआ था। दक्षिण में नर्मदा के तटीय क्षेत्रों जैसे होशंगाबाद से लेकर उत्तर में कोटा तक के इलाकों पर परमार राज कर रहे थे।
note: Extent of the Paramara realm: Malwa, Bhopal, Vidisha and Udaypur, Hansol, Modasa, Mahudi; Hoshangabad on the Narmada to Kota.
gloss: In their long period of five centuries ambitious Paramara kings expanded their borders over a large area. Their kingdom spread with Malwa beyond Bhopal to Vidisha and Udaypur, in the west to areas like Hansol, Modasa and Mahudi. Paramaras ruled areas from Hoshangabad on the Narmada coast in the south to Kota in the north.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
की गाय का बलात् हरण किया, तब उन (वसिष्ठ) के प्रभाव से अग्निकुण्ड में से एक

वीर उत्पन्न हुआ जिसने अकेले ही शत्रु सैन्य का नाश किया ॥५॥

मारयित्वा परान्धेनुमानिन्ये स ततो मुनिः।

उवाच परमारा [ख्यः पा]थिवेंद्रो भविष्यसि ॥६॥

शत्रुओं को मार कर वह गाय को वापस ले आया, तब मुनि ने कहा--"तुम परमार

नाम से राजा होगे ॥६॥
note: Prashasti verses 5-6: a hero rose from the fire-pit through Vasishtha's power to recover the cow and was told he would be king named Paramara (Agnikula legend).
gloss: ... when (he) forcibly took away the cow, then through the influence of (Vasishtha) a hero arose from the fire-pit who alone destroyed the enemy army. Having killed the enemies he brought back the cow; then the sage said: 'You will be a king by the name Paramara.'
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
उस वंश में अखिल यज्ञ समूह से तूभ देवताओं के द्वारा जिसकी कीर्ति गाई जा रही

है व जो द्विज समूह में रत्न के समान हैं और जिसने अपने पराक्रम से उच्च राजत्व का

मान प्राप्त कर लिया है ऐसा उपेन्द्रराज (नरेश) हुआ ॥७॥
note: Verse 7: Upendraraja in that lineage.
gloss: In that lineage was born Upendraraja, whose fame is sung by the gods and who is like a jewel among the twice-born, and who by his valour has attained the dignity of high kingship.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
उसका पुत्र बैरिसिंह था जो राजारूपी हाथियों के लिये सिंह के समान था, जो

पराक्रमियों में सबसे बलवान था और जिसने चारों समुद्रों से युक्त पृथ्वी पर प्रशस्तियुक्त

जयस्तम्भ स्थापित किये !!८॥
note: Verse 8: his son Vairisimha set up victory pillars with prashastis on the earth.
gloss: His son was Vairisimha, who was like a lion to elephant-like kings, strongest among the valiant, and who set up victory pillars with prashastis on the earth bounded by the four seas.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
उसके श्री सीयक (उत्पन्न) हुआ जिसका पादपीठ पृथ्वी के नरेशों के मुकुटों के

रत्नप्रभा से रंजित होता था तथा जिसकी तलवार की जल लहरियों में शत्रुसमूह डूब

जाते थे, जो विजयी राजाओं में सर्वश्रेष्ठ था ॥९॥

तस्माद्वन्ति तरूणीय नारविन्दभारवान्भूत्करकृपाणगरीचिदीपः।

श्रीवाक्यपतिः स (श) तमरवान्कृतितुरंगा गंगासमुद्र सलिलानि पि वन्ति यस्मै ॥१०॥

उससे श्री वाक्यपति हुआ जो अवन्ति की युवतियों के नयन कमलों के लिये सूर्य के समान था, अपने हाथ की तलवार की चमक से जो स्वयं प्रकाशमान था, जो इन्द्र के समान था तथा जिसके अक्ष गंगा व समुद्र के जलों का पान करते थे ॥१०॥
note: Prashasti verses 9-10: Siyaka, supreme among victorious kings, and his successor Vakpati.
gloss: From him was born Shri Siyaka, whose footstool was coloured by the jewel-radiance of the crowns of the kings of the earth and in whose sword's water-waves enemy hosts drowned, the foremost of victorious kings. From him came Shri Vakpati, who was like the sun to the lotus-eyes of the young women of Avanti, self-radiant with the gleam of the sword in his hand, like Indra, and whose horses drank the waters of the Ganga and the sea.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
उसका पुत्र जो संपूर्ण पृथ्वी के लिये आभूषण रूप था, जो गुणों का एकमात्र आश्रय था, शौर्य से जीते समस्त शत्रुओं से धन प्राप्ति के द्वारा जिसके कोप में वृद्धि होती थी, जो वकृत्य, उच्च कवित्व, तर्क प्रवीणता तथा शास्त्र आगम में निष्णात था तथा सज्जनों के द्वारा श्रीमत् वाक्यपतिराजदेव के नाम से जिसकी कीर्ति गाई जाती है ॥१३॥

कर्णाटलाटकैरल चोलशिरोरन्तरागिपदकमलः।

यशः प्रणीयगणार्थितदाता कल्पवृक्षप्रख्यः ॥१४॥

जिसके पदकमल कर्णाट लाट केरल चोल (नरेशों) के मुकुट रत्नों से रंजित होते थे और जो प्रार्थना करने वाले याचकों की इच्छा पूर्ति के लिये कल्पवृक्ष के समान विख्यात था ॥१४॥
note: Verse 13-14: Vakpatirajadeva praised as learned in rhetoric, poetry, logic and scripture, his feet coloured by crowns of Karnata, Lata, Kerala and Chola kings.
gloss: His son, an ornament for the whole earth, sole refuge of virtues, whose wrath grew by wealth taken from enemies conquered in valour, skilled in oratory, high poetry, logic and the scriptures, whose fame is sung by good men by the name of Shrimat Vakpatirajadeva. Whose lotus feet were coloured by the crown jewels of Karnata, Lata, Kerala and Chola kings, and who was known as a wish-fulfilling tree for petitioners.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: त्रिपुरी नगरी में विजय की इच्छा करने वाले उसने युद्ध में युवराज को जीतकर तथा उसके सेनापतियों को मार कर अपनी खड्ग को ऊंचा किया ॥१५॥
note: Verse 15: he defeated the Yuvaraja and killed his commanders at Tripuri.
gloss: Desiring victory at the city of Tripuri, he defeated the Yuvaraja in battle, killed his commanders and raised his sword high.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: उसके छोटे भाई श्री सिंधुराज ने हूणराज को जीत कर विजयश्री प्राप्त की, जिससे भोजराज उत्पन्न हुआ, जिसने उत्तम व्यक्तियों को भी कंपा दिया व जो अद्वितीय रत्न था ॥१६॥
note: Verse 16: Sindhuraja, the younger brother, defeated the Huna king; Bhoja was born to him.
gloss: His younger brother Shri Sindhuraja won victory by conquering the Huna king, from whom was born Bhojaraja, who made even excellent men tremble and who was a unique jewel.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: भोज सिर्फ एक राजा नहीं थे। वे कई विषयों के गहन ज्ञाता और विद्वान भी थे। व्याकरण, भाषा, साहित्य, नाटक, नृत्य, संगीत, जल प्रबंधन, वास्तु, नगर नियोजन, मंदिर निर्माण, स्थापत्य जैसे तमाम विषयों के विद्वानों की एक बड़ी प्रसिद्ध परिषद थी, जिसमें शामिल होने के लिए कश्मीर तक के विद्वानों में होड़ रहती थी।
note: Bhoja as scholar of many subjects (grammar, literature, drama, music, water management, vastu, town planning, temple building) with a famed council of scholars.
gloss: Bhoja was not just a king; he was also a deep scholar of many subjects. There was a famous council of scholars of grammar, language, literature, drama, dance, music, water management, vastu, town planning, temple building and architecture, which scholars even from Kashmir competed to join.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
की तरह हर तरह की कलाओं को अपने राज्य में विकसित किया। गुण संपन्न लोगों

को अपने आसपास सम्मान से जगह दी। शानदार निर्माण कराए। किताबें लिखीं।

सरस्वती कंठाभरण जैसे ज्ञान के केंद्र नई पीढ़ी को गढ़ने के लिए स्थापित किए।
note: Author's assessment of Bhoja's legacy: fostered arts, honoured the talented, built, wrote books, founded Sarasvati Kanthabharana centres of learning.
gloss: Like an ideal ruler Bhoja developed all kinds of arts in his kingdom. He gave honourable place around him to people of merit. He had splendid buildings made. He wrote books. He established centres of knowledge like Sarasvati Kanthabharana to shape the new generation.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: इस बात के काफी सबूत हैं कि भोपाल को राजा भोज ने बसाया था। बड़ा तालाब उन्हीं के बनाए मानव निर्मित बांध पर 36 वर्ग किलोमीटर में आज भी फैला हुआ है।
note: Author states there is considerable evidence Bhoja founded Bhopal; the Bada Talab lies on his man-made dam.
gloss: There is considerable evidence that Bhopal was settled by Raja Bhoj. The Bada Talab still spreads over 36 square kilometres on the man-made dam built by him.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: राजा भोज का ग्रंथ ‘समरांगण सूत्रधार’ इस बात की गवाही है कि वे किस ऊंचे दर्जे की रचनात्मकता को प्रश्रय देने वाले विद्वान थे। परमार राजाओं में भोज की हैसियत सितारों के बीच चमकते सूर्य जैसी है। उन्होंने उज्जैन, मांडू और धार में सरस्वती कंठाभरण बनवाए थे, जो सरस्वती के मंदिर और संस्कृत भाषा समेत अपने समय की ज्ञान की सभी विधाओं के शिक्षा केंद्र थे। मांडू तब मंडपदुर्ग के नाम से प्रसिद्ध था और वहां के सरस्वती कंठाभरण के एक छात्रावास के प्रभारी का नाम गोविंद भट्ट तक इतिहास में दर्ज है।
note: Bhoja's 'Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra' testifies to his patronage of creativity; he built Sarasvatī Kaṇṭhābharaṇa centres at Ujjain, Māṇḍū and Dhār.
gloss: King Bhoja's treatise 'Samarangana Sutradhara' is evidence of what high level of creativity he patronised as a scholar. Among Paramara kings Bhoja's stature is like the sun shining among stars. He had Sarasvati Kanthabharana built in Ujjain, Mandu and Dhar, which were temples of Sarasvati and centres of learning in all branches of knowledge of the time including the Sanskrit language. Mandu was then known as Mandapadurga, and the name of the head of one hostel of the Sarasvati Kanthabharana there, Govinda Bhatta, is recorded in history.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
जिसने कैलाश से मलय तक तथा उदयाचल से अस्ताचल तक संपूर्ण पृथ्वी का पृथुराज के समान उपभोग किया, जिसने अपने धनुष की डोरी से सहज ही में दिक्पालों को उखाड़ कर दिशाओं में फेंक दिया तथा जिसने पृथ्वी को परमप्रीति से प्रसन्न किया ॥१७॥

साधितं विहितं दत्तं ज्ञातं तथान्य केनचित्।

किमन्यत्कविराजस्य श्रीभोजस्य प्रशस्यते ॥१८॥

जो उसने साधित किया (प्राप्त किया), जो आदेश किया, जो दिया, जो ज्ञात किया वह कोई न कर सका। कविराज श्री भोज की इससे अधिक प्रशंसा क्या हो सकती है ॥१८॥
note: Verses 17-18: Bhoja enjoyed the whole earth from Kailasa to Malaya; the poet-king praised as unmatched.
gloss: He who enjoyed the entire earth from Kailasa to Malaya and from the rising mountain to the setting mountain like Prithu, who easily uprooted the guardians of the directions with his bowstring and threw them in the directions, and who gladdened the earth with supreme love. What he achieved, ordained, gave and knew, none else could do. What more praise can there be of Kaviraja Shri Bhoja.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: कर्णाट, लाटपति, गुर्जर नरेश व तुर्कों, जिनमें मुख्य चेदि नरेश इन्द्रथ, तोगल तथा भीम थे, की सेनाओं को जिसके भृत्यमात्रों ने ही विजित कर लिया व इस कारण जिसके पारंपरिक सेनाओं के बाहुबल की उन्नता की गणना की जाती है, उसके योद्धाओं की नहीं की जाती (क्योंकि योद्धाओं की तो अभी बारी भी नहीं आ पाई थी) ॥१९॥
note: Verse 19: forces of Chedi, Karnata, Lata, Gurjara kings and Turks defeated merely by Bhoja's servants.
gloss: The armies of the Karnata, the lord of Lata, the Gurjara king and the Turks, chiefly the Chedi king Indratha, Togala and Bhima, were conquered by his mere servants, and so the strength of his traditional armies is counted, not that of his warriors (since the warriors had not yet had their turn).
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: उस दौर में राजपरिवार के अन्य महत्वपूर्ण सदस्यों को राजधानी से दूर के महत्वपूर्ण नगरों और सैन्य ठिकानों की कमान सौंपी जाती थी। एक तरह से राज्य शासन चलाने के पारिवारिक प्रशिक्षण का यह हिस्सा था और उत्तराधिकारियों को राज्यकार्य में दक्ष ऐसे ही बनाया जाता होगा। जैसे मध्य में सम्राट बनने के पहले अशोक के पिता बिंदुसार ने उन्हें अवंति का राज्यपाल बनाकर उज्जैन भेजा था।
note: Royal-family members were given command of distant important towns and military posts as training in governance; author compares Ashoka at Ujjain.
gloss: In that period other important members of the royal family were entrusted with command of important towns and military bases far from the capital. In a way this was part of family training in running the state. Just as before becoming emperor Ashoka was sent to Ujjain by his father Bindusara as governor of Avanti.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: यह परमार राजाओं के महान कृतित्व की कहानी है, जिसकी शान में उदयादित्य नाम के राजा भोज के उत्तराधिकारी ने चार चांद लगा दिए थे।
note: Describes Udayaditya as Bhoja's successor who added lustre to Paramara achievement.
gloss: This is the story of the great works of the Paramara kings, to whose glory Udayaditya, a successor of King Bhoja, added lustre.

claim.value: successor of Bhoja (utpadhikari)

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: आखिर उदयपुर का भी तो राजा भोज से गहरा रिश्ता है। उदयादित्य उनके ही बाद में तो महाराजा हुए थे। उदयपुर के विकास की हर रूपरेखा से भोज भलीभांति अवगत रहे होंगे। उदयादित्य ने उनके ही संरक्षण में खुद को अपनी समृद्ध अभिरुचियों के साथ कुशल राजकाज के लिए तैयार किया होगा।
note: Author states Udaypur's deep relation with Bhoja; Udayaditya became maharaja after him and likely prepared under his patronage (conjecture).
gloss: After all, Udaipur too has a deep relationship with Raja Bhoj. Udayaditya became maharaja after him. Bhoj must have been well aware of every outline of Udaipur's development. Udayaditya must have prepared himself for skilled governance with his rich interests under Bhoj's patronage.

claim.value: became maharaja after Bhoja; prepared under his patronage (author's conjecture)

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: जिन राजा उदयदित्य के नाम पर इस नगर का नामकरण हुआ, वे परमार राजवंश के 12 वें राजा हैं। राजा भोज के बंधु हैं। यानी राजकाज के तौर-तरीके उन्होंने राजा भोज के साथ ही सीखे-समझे होंगे और जब राजा भोज राजधानी धार से अपना साम्राज्य देखते होंगे तब उदयदित्य को यहां का सामंत बनाकर भेजा गया होगा।
note: Author calls Udayāditya the 12th Paramāra king and Bhoja's brother, inferring he learned statecraft with Bhoja and was sent here as feudatory.
gloss: King Udayaditya, after whom this town is named, is the 12th king of the Paramara dynasty. He is King Bhoja's brother. That is, he must have learned and understood the ways of governance along with King Bhoja, and when King Bhoja was overseeing his empire from the capital Dhar, Udayaditya must have been sent here as feudatory.

claim.value: brother of Bhoja (author's statement); 12th Paramāra king

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
यह भी परमारों के दूसरे शिलालेखों की तरह शिव की आराधना से शुरू है और आगे उदयাদित्य के बारे में बताना शुरू कर देता है। हर शिलालेख कुछ नई जानकारी देता है। कुछ अलग इशारे करता है। यह भोज और उदयাদित्य के बीच के समय की धुंध में अस्पष्ट से दिखाई देने वाले संबंधों पर नई रोशनी डालता है।

इसके दूसरे श्लोक में है-"श्रीमान पावर (परमार) वंश नरेश सूरवीर मालव राज्य स्थापित करने वाला विद्वान नरेश हुआ जो पापियों को दण्डित करता था। उससे प्रसिद्ध पुत्र सकल गुणों से युक्त गांडल (गोंडल) नामक देवभक्त, दाना, भोक्ता, विवेकी और समस्त शत्रुओं को जीत वाला, अपनी कीर्ति से विख्यात हुआ।"
note: This record begins with Shiva worship and turns to Udayaditya; its verses 2 and 3 give a genealogy of a Paramara king and his son Gandal as quoted by the author.
gloss: Like other Paramara inscriptions it begins with worship of Shiva and goes on to tell about Udayaditya. Each inscription gives some new information. It throws new light on the relation between Bhoja and Udayaditya, seen faintly in the haze of time. Its second verse says a heroic, learned Paramara king established the Malwa kingdom and punished sinners. From him a renowned son named Gandal (Gondal), devout, generous, discerning, who conquered all enemies, became famous for his glory.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: यह भी हो सकता है कि जब कल्याणी के चालुक्यों और कर्णटों की संयुक्त सेनाओं ने राजधानी धारा पर हमलाकर भोजदेव के पुत्र और उत्तराधिकारी जयसिंह प्रथम को 1070 ई. के आसपास युद्ध में मार दिया हो तो ऐसी स्थिति में अचानक पैदा हुए राजनीतिक खालीपन में उदयাদित्य सिंहासन पर आए हों। यह सवाल और अहम है कि उदयাদित्य का राजा भोज से रिश्ता क्या था?
note: Possibility raised that after Jayasimha I was killed around 1070 CE by Chalukyas of Kalyani and Karnatas attacking Dhara, Udayaditya came to the throne in the political vacuum.
gloss: It may also be that when the combined armies of the Chalukyas of Kalyani and the Karnatas attacked the capital Dhara and killed Bhoja's son and successor Jayasimha I around 1070 CE, Udayaditya came to the throne in the sudden political vacuum. The question of Udayaditya's relation to Raja Bhoja is more important.

claim.value: possible accession after Jayasimha I's death c. 1070 (suggested, not stated)

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: वे कहते हैं कि उदयাদित्य के पिता के रूप में इन 'पाता' अथवा 'ज्ञाता' का जिक्र नए इशारे करने वाला बिंदु है। इसका एक मतलब यह है कि उदयাদित्य सिंधुराज की वंशपरम्परा से नहीं आ रहे थे बल्कि परमार राजवंश की एक अवर-शाखा से संबंधित थे। इसके आधार पर ऐसा माना जा सकता है कि उदयাদित्य संभवतः महाराजा भोज के अधीन एक सामंतान्धिपति के रूप में मालवा के पूर्वी भाग में राज करते थे। इस इलाके में विदिशा भी था। तब उदयपुर इसके अंतर्गत एक महत्वपूर्ण केंद्र के रूप में विकसित होने लगा होगा।
note: Verma's analysis: Udayaditya's father named as Pata/Jnata points to a junior Paramara branch, not Sindhuraja's line; possibly a feudatory of Bhoja ruling eastern Malwa including Vidisha, with Udaypur developing as an important centre.
gloss: Verma stops here to analyse. He says that the mention of 'Pata' or 'Jnata' as Udayaditya's father is a point suggesting new indications. One meaning is that Udayaditya did not descend from Sindhuraja's line but belonged to a junior branch of the Paramara dynasty. On this basis it can be assumed that Udayaditya probably ruled in the eastern part of Malwa as a chief feudatory under Maharaja Bhoja. Vidisha was also in this region. Then Udaypur must have begun to develop under it as an important centre.

claim.value: junior Paramara branch, not Sindhuraja's line; probable feudatory of Bhoja (Verma)

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
तीसरे श्लोक में है-"उसके पुत्र पाता (ज्ञाता) ने शत्रुसैन्यों का मंथन कर (अरिवलमथन) राज्य प्राप्त किया व वंश के पूर्वजों के अनुसार कीर्ति प्राप्त की। भूमंडल पर मध्यदेश मालव में जाकर प्रसिद्धि प्राप्त की, शाखानुकूल गति वाला, देवपूजक, धर्म तपस्या करके, जलाशय से युक्त देवालयों का निर्माण किया।"

पांचवा श्लोक कहता है-"ब्राह्मणों को सुवर्ण धान्य का अतिदान देने वाला, उदयাদित्य को योग्य मान कर नरेश बनाया व कीर्ति का संचय किया।"
note: Verses 3 and 5 as quoted: the father (Pata/Jnata) won a kingdom and built water-furnished temples; Udayaditya was deemed worthy and made king.
gloss: In the third verse: his son Pata (Jnata) crushed enemy armies, obtained the kingdom and gained fame like his forefathers; he built temples with reservoirs. The fifth verse says: giver of abundant gold and grain to Brahmins, he regarded Udayaditya as worthy, made him king and accumulated fame.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
अर्थात् "शिवभक्त (भोजदेव), जिसका प्रताप सूर्य के समान था, के स्वर्ग चले जाने पर, धारा नगरी के समान जब सारी पृथ्वी शत्रुरूपी अंधकार से व्याप्त हो गई तथा उसके पारंपरिक योद्धाजन दुर्बल हो गये, तब सूर्य के समान उदयादित्यदेव,

उन्नत शत्रूपी अंधकार को खड्गदण्ड की किरणों से नष्ट कर समस्तजनों के मनो को आनन्दित करता हुआ, उदित हुआ।
note: Translation of Udaypur prashasti verse 21: after Bhoja's death the earth was covered in darkness of enemies and Udayaditya rose like the sun. (Sanskrit lines in this chunk are OCR-damaged.)
gloss: After the Shiva-devotee (Bhojadeva), whose glory was like the sun, went to heaven, when the whole earth like the city of Dhara was covered by the darkness of enemies and his traditional warriors had grown weak, then Udayadityadeva, like the sun, rose, destroying the towering darkness of enemies with the rays of his sword and gladdening all people.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: ऐसी ही एक और कड़ी जुड़ती है उदयादित्य के शोरगढ़ अभिलेख से। इसकी पांचवीं और छठवीं पंक्ति में कहा गया है कि "परमभट्टारक महाराजाधिराज परमेश्वर श्री भोजदेव पादानुध्येत परमभट्टारक महाराजाधिराज परमेश्वर श्री उदयादित्यदेव : कुशली।"
note: Shorgarh inscription of Udayaditya, lines 5-6, calls him 'meditating on the feet of' Bhojadeva.
gloss: Another link is added by Udayaditya's Shorgarh inscription. Its fifth and sixth lines say: 'Paramabhattaraka Maharajadhiraja Parameshvara Shri Bhojadeva-padanudhyata Paramabhattaraka Maharajadhiraja Parameshvara Shri Udayadityadeva: well.'

claim.value: Shorgarh: 'Bhojadeva-padanudhyata'

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
गुप्त काल में पहले इतिहासकारों का मानना था कि 'ततपादानुध्येत' शब्द सीधे उत्तराधिकारी की बात करता है। जैसे चंद्रगुप्त प्रथम, समुद्रगुप्त, चंद्रगुप्त द्वितीय विक्रमादित्य, कुमारगुप्त, स्कंदगुप्त और उसके आगे की वंश परंपरा में हर परवर्ती शासक स्वयं को अपने पूर्ववर्ती का तत पादानुध्येत कह कर संबोधित करता है।

परंतु काकनादबोट (साँची) और उदयगिरि के लेखों में क्रमशः आत्रकादवर्द और वीरसेन शाब को चंद्रगुप्त द्वितीय विक्रमादित्य का ततपादानुध्येत कहा गया जो सम्राट के विश्वस्त कमांडर थे। इससे यह माना गया कि इसका शब्दिक अर्थ "चरणों का ध्यान करता हुआ" अधिक उपयुक्त है। यह तारीफ का कसीदा है, जिसका उत्तराधिकार से कोई लेना-देना नहीं। इसलिए यहाँ शोरगढ़ अभिलेख से भोज से उदयादित्य को सीधे उत्तराधिकार मिलने का दावा कमजोर पड़ जाता है।
note: Argues 'padanudhyata' means 'meditating on the feet' (praise), not succession, so the Shorgarh claim of direct succession from Bhoja is weakened; Gupta-era usage is cited.
gloss: Earlier historians of the Gupta period believed that 'tatpadanudhyata' speaks directly of a successor. But in the Kakanadabota (Sanchi) and Udayagiri inscriptions, Atrakadavarda and Virasena Shaba are called tatpadanudhyata of Chandragupta II, who were trusted commanders. Hence the literal meaning 'meditating on the feet' was considered more apt; it is praise with no relation to succession. So the claim of direct succession from Bhoja to Udayaditya weakens here.

claim.value: padanudhyata = praise, not direct succession (as argued)

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
उदयादित्य के सबसे छोटे पुत्र जगदेव के जैनड अभिलेख के श्लोक-6 में है-

यस्योदयादित्य नृपः पितासी, देवः पितृव्यः स च भोजराजः ।

विरेजतुयौ वसुधाधिपत्य, प्रास प्रतिष्ठानिव पुष्पवन्तो ॥6॥

इसका मतलब है- "जिसके पिता उदयादित्य थे और देव भोजराज पितृव्य अर्थात चाचा थे, विकसित होने वाले ये दोनों शिग्र ही अपने तेज से वसुधा का आधिपत्य प्राप्त कर प्रतिष्ठित हुए।"
note: Jainad inscription of Udayaditya's youngest son Jagadeva (verse 6) calls Udayaditya his father and Bhojaraja his paternal uncle (pitrivya).
gloss: In verse 6 of the Jainad inscription of Jagadeva, Udayaditya's youngest son: 'He whose father was Udayaditya and whose uncle (pitrivya) was the divine Bhojaraja.' It means: 'Whose father was Udayaditya, and the god Bhojaraja was the paternal uncle; these two, growing brilliant, attained sovereignty over the earth by their own splendour and were established.'

claim.value: Bhoja was paternal uncle (pitrivya) - Jainad inscription v.6 of Jagadeva

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: नागपुर अभिलेख राजा उदयादित्य के पुत्र राजा नरवर्मन का है जो उदयादित्य के बाद 1094 में परमार वंश के अगले राजा हुए और 1133 ई० तक शासन किया। इसमें परमार राजवंश की नरवर्मन तक की पूरी जानकारी है कि कौन किसके बाद सिंहासन पर आया। 56 वें श्लोक में साफ है कि यह प्रशस्ति स्वयं राजा नरवर्मन के द्वारा रची गई थी।
note: Nagpur inscription belongs to Naravarman, son of Udayaditya, who became the next Paramara king in 1094 and ruled to 1133; it gives the dynasty's succession up to him and was composed by Naravarman himself (verse 56).
gloss: The Nagpur inscription is of King Naravarman, son of King Udayaditya, who became the next king of the Paramara dynasty in 1094 after Udayaditya and ruled until 1133 CE. It has full information on the Paramara dynasty up to Naravarman, who succeeded whom. Verse 56 makes clear that this prashasti was composed by King Naravarman himself.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: अर्थात् "उस (भोजदेव) के इन्द्र की बंधुता को प्राप्त (दिवंगत) होने पर और राज्यस्वामी के कौटुम्बिकों के संघर्षरूपी जल में मग्न होने पर, उसका बंधु उदयादित्य नरेश हुआ, जिसने महासागर के समान संयुक्त रूप से कर्णाट कर्ण आदि नृपतियों के द्वारा पीड़ित इस पृथ्वी का उद्धार कर के वराह अवतार का अनुकरण किया। इसमें उदयादित्य को भोजदेव का "बंधु" बताया गया है। यह ध्यान देने योग्य शब्द है। धर्मशास्त्र में तीन प्रकार के बंधु हैं-आत्मबन्धु, पितृबन्धु और मातृबन्धु। इसके अलावा नातेदार, भाई-बिरादरी, सम्बन्धी, पारिवारिक नातेदार भी बंधु कहलाते हैं।
note: Nagpur prashasti verse 32 of Naravarman, translated: Udayaditya, 'bandhu' of Bhoja, rescued the earth afflicted by Karna and other kings; the author notes the word 'bandhu' has several senses.
gloss: After he (Bhojadeva) attained the kinship of Indra and the lord of the kingdom's kinsmen were sunk in the water of conflict, his bandhu Udayaditya became king, who, like the Varaha incarnation, rescued the earth troubled by the Karnata Karna and others joined like an ocean. Here Udayaditya is called Bhojadeva's 'bandhu'. This is a noteworthy word. In dharmashastra there are three kinds of bandhu: atmabandhu, pitribandhu and matribandhu. Besides, relatives, brotherhood and family kin are also called bandhu.

claim.value: 'bandhu' of Bhoja (Nagpur praśasti v.32)

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
अर्थात् "उन (भोज देव) के पश्चात् उनके भाई उदयदित्य वृद्धि को प्राप्त हुए, जिनने

मालव भूमि का उद्धार किया, जो तीन शत्रुओं के आक्रमण से (धूली में) मन हो गई

थी।"

जैनड लेख में जगदेव ने राजा उदयदित्य को अपना पिता व राजा भोजदेव

को चाचा (पितृव्य:) लिखा जबकि डोंगरगांव अभिलेख में जगदेव ने अपने पिता

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: जहां तक उदयपुर की बात है तो इसके नाम से ही जाहिर है कि यह राजा उदयादित्य से संबंधित है। पूर्ववर्ती परमार राजाओं के किसी भी अभिलेख का यहां न मिलना यह बताता है कि यह नगर उदयादित्य के समय में ही अस्तित्व में आया।
note: Argues the name itself shows Udaypur is connected with Udayaditya; absence of earlier Paramara records shows the town came into existence in his time.
gloss: As far as Udaypur is concerned, its very name shows it is related to King Udayaditya. That no inscription of earlier Paramara kings is found here shows that this town came into existence in Udayaditya's time.

claim.value: founded in Udayaditya's time; named after him; no earlier Paramara records here

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: पहली से छठवी पंक्ति में उदयादित्य की कुछ महत्वपूर्ण सैन्य विजयों का वर्णन है। इन विजितों में नाम केवल ढाहलमण्डल के चेदि शासक "ढाहलाधीश" का ही है। शिलालेख में दर्ज है कि ढहलाधीश को हराकर मार डाला गया। ढाहल मूलतः जबलपुर के आसपास का इलाका था जो कलचुरियों का मूलस्थान माना जाता है।
note: Lines 1-6 describe Udayaditya's military victories; the only named one is the Chedi ruler 'Dhahaladhisha', defeated and killed; Dhahala is around Jabalpur, thought the Kalachuri homeland.
gloss: Lines one to six describe some important military victories of Udayaditya. Among these conquered the name only of the Chedi ruler of Dhahala-mandala, the 'Dhahaladhisha', is given. It is recorded in the inscription that the Dhahaladhisha was defeated and killed. Dhahala was originally the area around Jabalpur, which is considered the original home of the Kalachuris.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: इस पर कोई तिथि अंकित नहीं है परन्तु इस अभिलेख से प्राप्त जानकारी के अनुसार यह राजा भोज के उत्तराधिकारी राजा उद्यादित्य के काल का प्रतीत होता है। राजा उद्यादित्य का शासनकाल 1070 से 1093 के बीच रहा।
note: The prashasti bears no date but appears from its content to be of Udayaditya's time; his reign is given as 1070 to 1093.
gloss: No date is marked on it but according to information from this inscription it appears to be of the time of King Udayaditya, successor of King Bhoja. King Udayaditya's reign was between 1070 and 1093.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: उदयपुर को उदयदित्य ने अपने पूरे मनोयोग से रचा था। राजा भोज के ये वंशज राज्य के इस आखिरी छोर का राज्यपाल थे। उसने उदयसागर बनवाया। नीलकंठेश्वर मंदिर खड़ा किया। देश के सुंदरतम देवालयों में से एक। स्थापत्य का बेजोड़ नमूना।
note: Shivkumar Vivek credits Udayaditya with creating Udaypur wholeheartedly, as a descendant of Bhoja and governor at the last edge of the kingdom; he built Udayasagar and the Nilakantheshwar temple, one of the most beautiful temples.
gloss: Udayaditya had created Udaypur with his full heart. This descendant of Raja Bhoja was the governor at this last edge of the state. He had Udayasagar built. He raised the Nilakantheshwar temple. One of the most beautiful temples of the country. A matchless specimen of architecture.

claim.value: Udayaditya created Udaypur; built Udayasagar and the temple (Vivek)

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: परमारों के राज में मंदिर सिर्फ पूजा-अनुष्ठान तक सीमित नहीं थे। वह स्थानीय स्तर पर एक नॉलेज सेंटर या पाठशालाओं के लिए भी उपयोग होते थे। बच्चों को वहीं अपने समय की समस्त विधाओं की शिक्षा दी जाती थी। धार, उज्जैन और मांडू के सरस्वती कंठाभरण इसके प्रमाण रहे हैं। चौक बाजार में पुराने भोपाल का ऐतिहासिक सभा मंडल भी, जो इसी उदयपुर के रचयिता और परमारों के राजवंश में राजा भोज के बाद हुए महाराज उदयादित्य ने ही बनवाया था।
note: Under the Paramaras temples were also local knowledge centres and schools, as the Saraswati Kanthabharanas show; the Sabha Mandal of old Bhopal was built by Udayaditya, creator of this Udaipur.
gloss: Under Paramara rule temples were not limited to worship and rituals. At the local level they were also used as knowledge centres or schools. Children were taught there all the disciplines of their time. The Saraswati Kanthabharanas of Dhar, Ujjain and Mandu have been proof of this. The historic Sabha Mandal of old Bhopal in Chowk Bazaar was also built by Maharaja Udayaditya, the maker of this very Udaipur, who came after Raja Bhoj in the Paramara dynasty.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: परमार जिस नौवीं से चौदहवीं सदी के दौरान इस इलाके में हुए, वह समय ही ऐसा था जब पूरे भारत में मौजूद राजवंश अपने राज्यों में बेहतरीन निर्माण कार्य कर रहे थे। दूर दक्षिण में चोलों से लेकर बुंदेलखंड के चंदेलों तक, राजस्थान में चौहानों से लेकर बंगाल-बिहार में पाल राजाओं तक पीढ़ियों के योगदान से निर्मित बेशाकीमती विरासत अपने चरम पर चमक रही थी।
note: Author places the Paramāras (ninth to fourteenth century) in a period of intense temple-building across Indian dynasties.
gloss: The period from the ninth to the fourteenth century in which the Paramāras flourished in this region was a time when dynasties across India were doing excellent construction in their kingdoms. From the Cholas far in the south to the Chandellas of Bundelkhand, from the Chauhans in Rajasthan to the Pala kings in Bengal-Bihar, the precious heritage built by generations was shining at its peak.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: भूमिपूजन, शिलान्यास और गर्भगृह में अभिषेक का वह उत्सव, जब महाराज उदयादित्य स्वयं अपने मंत्रियों सहित सपरिवार यहां उपस्थित थे। धारा नगरी, उज्जयिनी, मंडपदुर्ग और भोपाल से भी अनेक प्रमुख सामंत और शिल्पी अपने शिष्यों के साथ यहां आए थे।
note: Imagined narration of the temple's foundation ceremony attended by Udayaditya, feudatories and craftsmen from Dhara, Ujjain, Mandapadurga and Bhopal (literary reconstruction, not cited evidence).
gloss: The festival of bhumipujan, foundation-laying and abhisheka in the sanctum, when Maharaj Udayaditya himself was present with ministers and family. Many chief feudatories and craftsmen with their pupils came from Dhara city, Ujjayini, Mandapadurga and Bhopal.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: परमार वंश के सभी राजा कलाप्रिय थे। मंदिरों के निर्माण पूरे राज्य में चलते थे। भोजपुर की चट्टान से लेकर धारा नगरी, उज्जयनी, मंडपदुर्ग और ओंकारेश्वर तक कितने नाम गिनाएं। अगर परमारों के राज में कोई सबसे व्यस्त था तो वे आदर्शीय शिल्पकार थे। वे पत्थरों पर आश्चर्य उकेरते थे।
note: Paramara kings were art-loving; temples built across the realm from Bhojpur to Dhara, Ujjayini, Mandapadurga and Omkareshwar; craftsmen busiest.
gloss: All kings of the Paramara dynasty were lovers of art. Temple construction went on across the kingdom: from the rock of Bhojpur to Dhara, Ujjayini, Mandapadurga and Omkareshwar. If anyone was busiest under Paramara rule it was the ideal craftsmen. They carved wonders in stone.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: कलाप्रिय परमार राजाओं की प्रतिष्ठा का एक कारण यह भी था कि बड़े ही विद्या अनुरागी थे। भाषा, व्याकरण, कविता, नाटक, वास्तु, स्थापत्य, ज्योतिष, संगीत जैसी तमाम विधाओं के जानकार उनके आसपास हुआ करते थे। राजा भोज तो इन प्रतिभाशाली कला विशेषज्ञों के बीच स्वयं एक विद्वान की हैसियत रखते थे। ऐसे माहौल में जिन उदयदित्य की परवरिश हुई होगी, उनके आसपास भी बिल्कुल वैसा ही माहौल होना ही चाहिए था।
note: Paramara kings were learned patrons with experts in language, grammar, poetry, drama, architecture, astrology and music around them; Udayaditya's upbringing presumed similar.
gloss: One reason for the repute of the art-loving Paramara kings was that they were great lovers of learning. Experts in language, grammar, poetry, drama, vastu, architecture, astrology and music were around them. Raja Bhoj himself was a scholar among these talents. The environment around Udayaditya, brought up in such an atmosphere, must have been the same.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: वैसे पहाड़ी ऊंचाइयों की बात करें तो ओंकारेश्वर और मंदाता में भी परमार राजाओं ने नर्मदा के तटों पर अपनी श्रद्धा शिल्प में प्रकट की थी। चंदेरी और ग्वालियर में भी पहाड़ों पर आस्था के स्मारक बनाए गए।
note: Paramara kings also expressed devotion in hill-top architecture at Omkareshwar and Mandhata on the Narmada; hill monuments of faith at Chanderi and Gwalior.
gloss: Speaking of hilltop heights, at Omkareshwar and Mandhata too the Paramara kings expressed their devotion in sculpture on the Narmada's banks. At Chanderi and Gwalior also monuments of faith were built on hills.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: वह एक चौकोर रचना में वास्तु के नियमों के तहत बसाया गया एक व्यवस्थित नगर था, जिसके बीचों-बीच आज का चौक बाजार रहा होगा। परमारों के समय यह सभामंडल था, नगर का महत्वपूर्ण ब्रह्मस्थान। यह एक विशाल मंदिर परिसर था, जो संस्कृत का विद्यालय भी था। बिल्कुल उज्जैन, धार और मांडू के महान् सरस्वती कंठाभरणों की तर्ज पर। लेकिन सभा मंडल का निर्माण भोज के बाद हुआ और उदयादित्य ने ही कराया।
note: Old Bhopal described as a vastu-planned square town with a Paramara-time Sabha Mandal temple-school; the Sabha Mandal was built after Bhoja by Udayaditya.
gloss: It was an orderly city settled in a square design under the rules of vastu, with today's Chowk Bazaar probably at its centre. In Paramara times this was the Sabha Mandal, the city's important Brahmasthana. It was a vast temple complex that was also a Sanskrit school, on the lines of the great Sarasvati Kanthabharanas of Ujjain, Dhar and Mandu. But the Sabha Mandal was built after Bhoja and was made by Udayaditya himself.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: पत्थर की प्रचुर मात्रा में उपलब्धता ने परमार राजवंश को यह अवसर दिया कि वे स्थापत्य के शानदार नमूने खड़े करें। इस काम में परमार राजाओं ने जैसे तमिलनाडू के चोल राजाओं से मुकाबला किया है। अपने राज्य में हर कहीं बेमिसाल मंदिर, महल, तालाब, बावड़ियां, संस्कृत के शिक्षा केंद्र बनवाए।
note: Abundant stone let the Paramāras raise architectural masterpieces, competing with the Cholas, and build temples, palaces, tanks, stepwells and Sanskrit learning centres.
gloss: The abundant availability of stone gave the Paramara dynasty the opportunity to raise splendid specimens of architecture. In this work the Paramara kings competed as it were with the Chola kings of Tamil Nadu. Everywhere in their kingdom they had matchless temples, palaces, tanks, stepwells and centres of Sanskrit learning built.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: यहीं रहकर अपने राजा के लिए सदैव शुभकामनाएं व्यक्त की हों और जब मंदिर का निर्माण पूर्ण हुआ होगा तब उसने 30 मार्च 1080 के ध्वजारोहण समारोह के समय राजा के रथों का इंतजार किया हो। उदयपुर के राजमहलों की वह रौनक भी आखिरी नहीं थी। ढाई सौ साल बाद तक उदयपुर ऐसा ही चमकता रहा था।
note: Author imagines the royal dancer awaiting the king's chariots at the flag-hoisting ceremony of 30 March 1080 on the temple's completion; Udaypur shone for another 250 years.
gloss: When the temple's construction was complete she may have waited for the king's chariots at the flag-hoisting ceremony of 30 March 1080. That splendour of Udaipur's palaces was not the last. Udaipur kept shining like this for another two and a half hundred years.

claim.value: 30 March 1080 flag-hoisting (author)

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: इस शिलालेख की बाद की पंक्तियों में परमारों के अधीन किन्हीं नेमक वंश के स्थानीय नरेशों का विवरण है। चूंकि उदयपुर सीधा परमार शासन के अंतर्गत था तो ऐसा कैसे मुमकिन है कि किसी और वंश का जिक्र आए। मुमकिन है कि राजा उदयादित्य ने अपने मातहत नेमक वंशीय किसी सामंत को यह इलाका सौंप रखा हो। इस अधूरे शिलालेख में हो सकता है कि नेमकों के बारे में और कुछ ब्यौरे भी रहे हों, लेकिन वे पढ़े जाने लायक नहीं बचे।
note: Later lines mention local rulers of the Nemaka lineage under the Paramaras; possibly Udayaditya gave the area to a Nemaka feudatory; the rest unreadable.
gloss: In the later lines of this inscription there is an account of local rulers of a Nemaka dynasty under the Paramaras. Since Udaypur was under direct Paramara rule, how could another dynasty be mentioned? It is possible that King Udayaditya had assigned this area to a feudatory of the Nemaka lineage. Perhaps this incomplete inscription had more details about the Nemakas, but they have not survived to be read.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: यह अभिलेख बताता है कि नेमक वंशीय शासक शिव के उपासक थे। शूद्रक नामक एक अन्य सामंत हुआ, जिसने किसी गुर्जर नरेश पर विजय प्राप्त की थी। इस अभिलेख में वर्णन है कि इसी शूद्रक नामक सामंत के पुत्र जिसका नाम अस्पष्ट है, ने उदयपुर में मंदिर का निर्माण करवाया था। हम यह अंदाजा ही लगा सकते हैं कि जिस समय उदयपुर मंदिर का निर्माण शुरू हुआ होगा, नेमक वंश का यह सामन्तकुल यहां का स्थानीय प्रशासक रहा हो और उसी की देखरेख में इस मंदिर का निर्माण हुआ हो।
note: Per the inscription, the unnamed son of the feudatory Shudraka (Nemaka lineage, Shiva worshippers) built a temple at Udaypur; the author conjectures this family were local administrators when construction began.
gloss: This inscription tells that the Nemaka-line rulers were worshippers of Shiva. Another feudatory named Shudraka defeated some Gurjara king. The inscription describes that the son of this Shudraka, whose name is unclear, had a temple built at Udaypur. We can only guess that when construction of the Udaypur temple began, this feudatory family of the Nemaka line may have been the local administrator here and the temple was built under its supervision.

claim.value: unnamed son of feudatory Shudraka (Nemaka line), per this inscription (author's reading)

tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote: हम अच्छी तरह से जानते हैं कि महात्वाकांक्षी परमार राजाओं की प्रसिद्धि उनकी वीरता और युद्ध विजयों के कारण ही नहीं है। उनके समय ज्ञान की सभी विधाओं को आसरा मिला। स्थापत्य के बेजोड़ स्मारक सदियों तक बनते ही रहे। इन स्मारकों के आसपास उज्जैन, धारा, मांडू, भोजपाल, विदिशा और उदयपुर तक बड़े नॉलेज सेंटर बने, जिन्हें इन राजाओं ने ऊंचाइयों तक पहुंचाया।
note: Paramara patronage of learning and monuments; knowledge centres at Ujjain, Dhara, Mandu, Bhojpal, Vidisha and Udaypur.
gloss: We know well that the fame of ambitious Paramara kings is not only for valour and conquests. In their time all branches of knowledge found shelter. Unmatched monuments of architecture were built for centuries. Around these monuments big knowledge centres arose up to Ujjain, Dhara, Mandu, Bhojpal, Vidisha and Udaypur, which these kings raised to heights.
tier_note: T8 tradition / testimony: testimony and local tradition (Tiwari); memory, not the event

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original

Before becoming king he must have held some military or administrative responsibility at Udaypur, and hence in this inscription he is addressed only by the title Mahakumara. If he lived at Udaypur before becoming king, this fact raises Udaypur's importance, because about a hundred and fifty years earlier Udayaditya too must have been in such a role. Now it also becomes clear that Udaypur was a centre from which at least two princes of the Paramara dynasty emerged as kings.

quote:
This made possible for the Rajput feudatory powers to assert their independence and as a result the new Rajput Houses of the Paramaras and the Kacchavahas first came into prominence dividing the territories of Madhya Bharat into the two sizeable kingdoms of Malwa and Gwalior respectively.

quote: Based on ancient relics, inscriptions, and corroborated historical evidence, the Parmars are traditionally regarded as belonging to the Agnikula (fire-born) lineage. According to Dr. Dasharatha Sharma, “No dynasty other than the Paramaras should be regarded as an Agnikula lineage; only the Parmars can be identified as the true Agnikula clan.” Archaeological findings from Vasantgarh, Udaipur, Nagpur, Harthal, Delwara, Patnarayan, Achaleshwar, and other sites further support this view.

quote: The original residence of the Parmaras is Malwa. And the branch there is believed to be the main branch of the Parmaras. As far as the boundaries of their kingdoms are concerned, the empire extends to the present-day states of Kota and Bundi in the north, parts of Bhilsa, Hoshangabad and Sagar Janapada in the east, up to the Godavari river and the territory of Khandesh in the south, and up to the Mahi river in the west.

quote: In a Sarvatobhadra town, Brahmanas and Kshatriyas should be settled in the east and the water-quarter. In the southeast (Agneya) direction, goldsmiths and other artisans who use fire should be settled. Vaishyas, gamblers, rogues and potters should be settled in the south; and there too actors and dancers should be settled. Swine-keepers, shepherds, hunters (those who do *mrigaya*), boatmen (*kevata*), and suppression-officers (police, *damanadhikari*) and the like should be settled in the southwest (Nairritya). People skilled in chariots or weapons should be settled in the west of the town. The abode of ascetics (*yati-sadana*), the assembly of young Brahmin students (*batuka*), the water-booth (*prapa*), the merit-hall (*punya-shala*) and the like should be in the north.

book_title: Geo-Heritage of Udaypur, Vidisha District, Madhya Pradesh: The Third Eye
quote:
At about 100 meters from this Natraj sculpture, we see a long wall that measures 1400 meters. It is a very thick wall encircling the hillock from all side, a close examination of this 1400 m wall show that this is a fortification wall, meaning that the encircled land is part of a fort complex, which existed prior to Udayaditya, or could have been constructed during the time of Udayaditya as a military Cantonment, because this was the most secured hillock, with very steep slopes.
Walking along this hill fortification wall, we see bastions of different dimensions, the semicircular bastion, the rectangular bastion, and gateways on both sides of the entry gate.
This entire fort complex is a mystery because historical records are silent about it. It is also an architectural marvel that is standing undisturbed over a span of 1400 meters, maybe the longest one anywhere in Madhya Pradesh.
note: 1400 m fortification wall with bastions and gateways; either pre-Udayaditya or a military cantonment of his time; historical records silent.
